note: Real full_synthesis output on the joinery memo. Receipts are heuristically derived from the source fragments, not emitted by the model — see pre-registered question 3.

items.statement: Positioning above mass-market quality, below premium pricing
items.receipt: Aiming above the IKEA/Caboodle ceiling on design quality while promising costs far below a full architect engagement

items.statement: Revenue model deliberately unresolved pending market validation
items.receipt: Revenue model deliberately unresolved

items.statement: Multiple potential customer types: architect, builder, or homeowner
items.receipt: Who pays is explicitly open — could be architect, builder or homeowner depending on circumstance

items.statement: Pricing structure undecided: project-based vs seat-based vs subscription
items.receipt: Possibly project-based rather than seat-based

items.statement: Strategic deferral of monetization decisions until demand confirmed
items.receipt: Decision consciously deferred until demand and feasibility are confirmed

items.statement: At diligence stage, not commitment stage
items.receipt: At the diligence stage, not the commitment stage

items.statement: Deliberate restraint on solution thinking before market confirmation
items.receipt: Explicit instruction to self not to get too far into solution thinking before confirming the market

items.statement: Core thesis: professional intermediaries migrating to SaaS-enabled self-service
items.receipt: Draws on a long-running thesis: work once done by professional intermediaries has migrated to SaaS-enabled self-service — travel via Airbnb, Booking.com and airline aggregators replacing Flight Centre consultants; accounting and tax prep via MYOB and Xero; freight and logistics; HR and hiring

items.statement: Strategic tension between full integrated-build (attractive) and standalone-kitchen (de-risked)
items.receipt: Most drawn to the full integrated-build version, but the standalone-kitchen segment is the easier de-risking start — and may be a different business against a much wider competitive field

items.statement: Standalone-kitchen may be a different business with wider competition
items.receipt: Most drawn to the full integrated-build version, but the standalone-kitchen segment is the easier de-risking start — and may be a different business against a much wider competitive field

items.statement: Founder-domain fit across software, design and cabinet making
items.receipt: Founder-domain fit across software, design and cabinet making

items.statement: Long software technology career combined with lifelong physical design interest
items.receipt: Long career in software technology, plus recent years working with a range of startup companies

items.statement: Direct hands-on experience across design, specification and installation
items.receipt: Founder-domain fit across software, design and cabinet making

items.statement: Two home renovations as first-hand source material
items.receipt: Two home renovations in the last ten years as direct source material

items.statement: Solo founder with no team, capital or tech assets currently in place
items.receipt: No team, capital, tech assets or IP position described.

items.statement: Confidence in ability to execute SaaS-based services business
items.receipt: Observation that spinning up a SaaS-based services business is not especially difficult and many such businesses do fine

items.statement: Architect-quality design at fraction of architect cost (80% benefit, orders of magnitude cheaper)
items.receipt: For the homeowner: an architect-quality design outcome at a fraction of full architect cost, competitive quotes, and an advocate on quality

items.statement: Above IKEA/Caboodle quality ceiling—interesting materials, not commodity finishes
items.receipt: Aimed above the IKEA/Caboodle ceiling — interesting materials, sourced from different places, integral to the project design, not Laminex with ABS edging

items.statement: Early, commitment-free joinery feasibility and pricing while design still flexible
items.receipt: Early, commitment-free joinery feasibility and price, plus a manufacture-ready specification

items.statement: Manufacture-ready specification in format wholesale shops already use
items.receipt: Produce a specification complete enough to manufacture from, in a format the wholesale shops already produce in

items.statement: Transparency in joinery numbers versus current builder opacity
items.receipt: Value depends on making the joinery number credible and transparent early, but today builders deliberately keep joinery estimates opaque to clients to protect margin

items.statement: Homeowner advocacy on quality plus competitive quotes
items.receipt: For the homeowner: an architect-quality design outcome at a fraction of full architect cost, competitive quotes, and an advocate on quality

items.statement: Detail gap between architect design and manufacturable joinery discovered too late
items.receipt: The detail gap between architect design and manufacturable joinery is discovered too late

items.statement: Cabinet maker is first party who can produce real numbers but only involved at pricing
items.receipt: The cabinet maker is the first party who can produce a real number, and only gets involved at pricing

items.statement: Predictable failure sequence: design, price shock, blame, shopping around, unpaid rework, delay
items.receipt: Typical failure sequence: architect produces the big idea, cabinet maker prices it, it is unaffordable, blame lands on the architect, client shops it around, client eventually discovers the design itself is what is expensive, rework follows, architect and cabinet maker collaborate on scope reductions they are largely unpaid for, project is delayed, all parties worse off

items.statement: Joinery is large line item (quarter of renovation) carried as provisional sum
items.receipt: Joinery is a large, poorly-estimated line item and the hardest trade for builders to schedule

items.statement: Cabinet makers absorb schedule slip and structural cost of unpaid specification work
items.receipt: Cabinet makers are one of the last trades in the sequence, so they absorb accumulated schedule slip; good ones are not idle and waiting for work

items.statement: Opportunity to provide design-and-feasibility role earlier without commitment
items.receipt: Reframed opportunity: provide the cabinet maker's design-and-feasibility role earlier in the process, with no commitment required from any party

items.statement: The primary professional incumbent is estimation by analogy, not a software product
items.receipt: The incumbent is estimation by analogy, not a product

items.statement: Professional estimates are opaque summary line items, not detailed specifications
items.receipt: Output is summary line items, roughly a one-pager per room of joinery, and not fully transparent to the client.

items.statement: Flat-pack systems offer accessibility but cap out below genuinely custom results
items.receipt: Flat-pack incumbents cap out below a genuinely custom result

items.statement: Consumers in flat-pack models take on design responsibility with limited experience
items.receipt: In that model the consumer takes on responsibility for design, and sometimes manufacture and installation, with limited experience

items.statement: A gap exists between opaque professional estimates and limited flat-pack outcomes
Design leakage — customers shopping the spec themselves
items.receipt: Design leakage — the customer shops the spec themselves

items.statement: Wholesale manufacturers win, joinery trade loses
items.receipt: The cabinet maker / joinery trade LOSES — today they either build cabinets or sub-contract boxes to the same wholesalers, plus install, and carry the design, quoting and architect-wrangling burden.

items.statement: Install layer risks deskilling and quality degradation
items.receipt: The joinery trade is disintermediated, and the install layer may degrade as a result

items.statement: Self-installation has real quality traps despite being possible
items.receipt: Self-installation has real quality traps

items.statement: Model depends on competent install while disintermediating installers
items.receipt: The wholesale manufacturer gains manufacture-ready jobs while the joinery trade that currently feeds and installs them is cut out — but the model still depends on competent install, which the same disintermediation may degrade

items.statement: Fundamental reframe from consumer self-service to architect/builder-led motion
items.receipt: The memo's original framing was consumer self-service replacing professionals; the reframe puts architects and builders in the driver's seat, which is close to the opposite motion

items.statement: Builders and architects as primary distribution channels, not yet designed
items.receipt: Channel implied through builders and architects, not yet designed

items.statement: Value depends on joinery cost transparency, but builders keep estimates opaque to protect margin
items.receipt: Value depends on making the joinery number credible and transparent early, but today builders deliberately keep joinery estimates opaque to clients to protect margin

items.statement: Builders can route clients away from expensive specialist kitchen companies
items.receipt: A builder could advise a client without an architect that a specialist kitchen design-supply-install company is expensive and creates coordination and liability headaches, then route them to this service

items.statement: Design-and-build firms less likely to engage since architect work already paid for
items.receipt: Builders doing design-and-build with their own architect partnerships are seen as less likely to engage, since that work is the architect's domain and already paid for by the client

items.statement: No acquisition, pricing-to-channel, or partnership motion defined
items.receipt: No acquisition, pricing-to-channel, or partnership motion described.

items.statement: The buyer identity is unsettled: homeowner, architect, or builder
items.receipt: Users may be professionals (architect, builder) rather than the homeowner; direct-to-consumer remains on the table, not resolved either way

items.statement: Original consumer self-service framing has been reframed to put professionals in the driver's seat
items.receipt: The memo's original framing was consumer self-service replacing professionals; the reframe puts architects and builders in the driver's seat, which is close to the opposite motion

items.statement: Target is joinery inside a larger build, not standalone kitchens
items.receipt: Target is joinery inside a larger build, not standalone kitchens — but the buyer is unsettled

items.statement: Standalone kitchen segment is easier de-risking but may be a different business
items.receipt: Segment 3 (standalone kitchen) judged the easiest de-risking start but possibly a different business facing a much wider field of existing solutions

items.statement: Most drawn to full integrated-build version despite de-risking logic
items.receipt: Most drawn to the full integrated-build version, but the standalone-kitchen segment is the easier de-risking start — and may be a different business against a much wider competitive field

items.statement: Segment definition shifted from absence of architect to build context
items.receipt: Segment 1 initially chosen as target, then reframed: the problem is present even when an architect IS involved, so the segment is defined by the build context rather than by absence of an architect

items.statement: Iterative, expert-supported design tool producing manufacture-ready specifications
items.receipt: Design tool to manufacture-ready spec, then bid out to wholesalers

items.statement: Bid-based marketplace connecting completed specs to wholesale manufacturers
Direct integration with professional workflows (Revit) and manufacturing systems (Mosaic CAD)
items.receipt: Professional version likely needs to sit in the architect's workflow — integration or import/export with tools like Revit

items.statement: Quality guarantees and consumer advocacy as value-adds
items.receipt: Possible quality guarantees and an advocacy role on the consumer's behalf

items.statement: Disintermediation of joinery trade while maintaining dependency on skilled installation
items.receipt: The wholesale manufacturer gains manufacture-ready jobs while the joinery trade that currently feeds and installs them is cut out — but the model still depends on competent install, which the same disintermediation may degrade

items.statement: Tension between solution detail and intent to avoid premature solution thinking
items.receipt: Explicit intent not to get ahead into solution thinking, alongside a fairly detailed solution already sketched (design tool, bidding marketplace, Revit integration, quality guarantees)
